prompt: In this lesson's rotation, who is the secondary for a given week?
hint: Who still remembers what was strange?

choices.text: The person who will be primary next week
choices.why: The rotation uses the week before, not the week after.

choices.text: Last week's primary
choices.why: Right. They still remember what was strange last week.

choices.text: The team's lead, every week
choices.why: The lead is the last step of the ladder, not the secondary.

choices.text: Whoever is awake when a page arrives
choices.why: A rotation names a person in advance, so nobody has to guess.

prompt: A weekly rotation has four people. In an eight-week period, how many weeks is each person primary?
Which line of a handoff note does this lesson call the most important?
hint: It is about the next person's incident.

choices.text: Whether anything was changed by hand
choices.why: Right. An unrecorded manual change causes the next person's incident.

choices.text: The number of pages in the week
choices.why: Useful, and visible on a dashboard; the note carries what is not.

choices.text: Who was slow to acknowledge a page
choices.why: A note is not a list of blame.

choices.text: The certificate renewal date
choices.why: Worth a line, but not the one the lesson singles out.

prompt: Google's SRE book puts a ceiling on incidents per twelve-hour on-call shift. What is it?
hint: An incident and its follow-up take most of a day.

prompt: What does acknowledging a page mean?

choices.text: The problem is fixed
choices.why: Fixing comes later; acknowledging comes in the first minutes.

choices.text: The alarm was a false one
choices.why: Acknowledging says nothing about whether the alarm was right.

choices.text: The secondary should take over
choices.why: That is what happens when nobody acknowledges.

choices.text: I have it
choices.why: Right. Someone owns it now, and the ladder stops.

prompt: Why does the ladder for the shop live in a paging service rather than in SNS?

choices.text: SNS cannot deliver a message to a phone number
choices.why: SNS sends SMS; what it lacks is something else.

choices.text: SNS is too expensive for pages
choices.why: Price is not the reason given.

choices.text: SNS hears nothing back from a reader
choices.why: Right. With no acknowledgement coming back, there is nothing to escalate on.

choices.text: SNS topics hold one subscription each
choices.why: A topic delivers to every subscription it has.

prompt: What should the last step of an escalation ladder page?
hint: Who answers a page sent to twelve people?

choices.text: One named person, such as the team's lead
choices.why: Right. A person, never a group.

choices.text: The whole engineering team at once, by e-mail and SMS
choices.why: Each of them expects another to answer.

choices.text: The customer support channel
choices.why: Support talks to customers; it does not own the system.

choices.text: The primary again, in a loop
choices.why: The primary already did not answer.

prompt: Match each of the four moves to the alarm it suits.

pairs.right: disk-80, filled every night by the backup's temporary files
An alarm that pages on a single five-minute spike
db-cpu, a cause that api-errors covers when it matters
An alarm nobody acted on in three months

prompt: Which of these should go to shop-ticket rather than shop-page?
hint: Can it wait for working hours?

choices.text: Checkout returning errors to customers
choices.why: Customers are affected now: that is a page.

choices.text: A certificate due to expire in three weeks
choices.why: Right. Work for the morning, not for three in the morning.

choices.text: Latency above the SLO for fifteen minutes
choices.why: Customers feel it now: a page.

choices.text: Error budget burning at fourteen times the rate
choices.why: Lesson 12's fast burn pages.

prompt: In the lesson's month, somebody acted on 23 of the 121 pages. What percentage is that? Round to the nearest whole number.
db-cpu sent 41 pages and somebody acted on 3. What percentage of its pages were acted on? Round to the nearest whole number.
Why does the lesson count pages at night apart from the total?
hint: What else does a night page cost?

choices.text: Pages at night are cheaper for the paging service
choices.why: Price has nothing to do with it.

choices.text: CloudWatch bills an alarm that fires at night separately
choices.why: It does not; alarms cost the same at any hour.

choices.text: A page at night costs the next day as well
choices.why: Right. The person is tired at work the day after.

choices.text: Customers are asleep at night
choices.why: Some are not, and that is not the lesson's reason.

prompt: The measure that orders alarms from most to least useful is the share of an alarm's pages that somebody ____ on. (one word)
Paging on symptoms only, the month drops from 121 pages to 30. What should be checked before making that change?

choices.text: Whether a symptom alarm would have paged anyway
choices.why: Right. If api-errors would have paged anyway, the cause alarm can be a ticket.

choices.text: Whether the paging service charges per page
choices.why: Cost is not the risk here.

choices.text: Whether the team agrees that those alarms are annoying at night
choices.why: Annoyance is not evidence.

choices.text: Whether moto evaluates the alarms correctly
choices.why: moto evaluates no alarm, and the month came from pages.csv.

prompt: Put the four moves for a noisy alarm in the order this lesson says to try them.
hint: Start with what removes the risk itself.

prompt: What does put-metric-alarm do when the alarm name already exists?
hint: Is there a command to change only the actions?

choices.text: It merges the new fields into the alarm
choices.why: There is no merge; that is why the lesson reads the alarm first.

choices.text: It refuses, because the name is taken
choices.why: It accepts the name and overwrites.

choices.text: It creates a second alarm with a suffix
choices.why: Alarm names are unique; it overwrites.

choices.text: It replaces the whole alarm
choices.why: Right. Every setting not given is gone.

prompt: The first put-metric-alarm from the jq filter was refused with 'Invalid type for parameter AlarmDescription, value: None'. What fixed it?

choices.text: Setting the alarm state to OK first
choices.why: The state is not an input to put-metric-alarm.

choices.text: Dropping the fields whose value is null
choices.why: Right. with_entries(select(.value != null)) removes the empty description.

choices.text: Using the console instead
choices.why: The command line works once the input is valid.

choices.text: Deleting the alarm and creating it again
choices.why: The input would still carry the null.

prompt: Why does the lesson test an alarm that never fires?

choices.text: To raise the count of pages somebody acted on this month
choices.why: A test page is not counted as a real one.

choices.text: Because AWS deletes an alarm that has not fired in a year
choices.why: It does not.

choices.text: A broken route is as silent as a healthy service
choices.why: Right. Only a test tells the two apart.

choices.text: To check that moto evaluates it
choices.why: moto evaluates nothing; the test is for AWS.

prompt: Which habits does the lesson give for keeping alarms tuned? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Count pages per alarm at the handoff
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Write in each alarm's description who acts and what they do
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Test the alarms that never fire
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Raise every threshold by ten percent each month
choices.why: A blanket change is not tuning; each alarm gets its own move.

choices.text: Page the whole team for every new alarm
choices.why: That is the fatigue the lesson measures.

prompt: After the tuning, the month has 30 pages in four weeks, and a shift is one week. How many pages does a primary receive in an average shift?
